name: Delhivery Ltd
title: Delhivery Ltd - 543529 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 volumes up 32% and PTL tonnage up 14.2%, with Express growth now at the low end of 20-30% guidance and Local ARR ahead of the revised 160-175 Cr path, though margins were flagged as the watch item.

triggers.label: Wage and diesel pass-through 96-97% automatic
triggers.quote:
96-97%

triggers.label: Local ARR crossed 200 Cr
triggers.quote: Local, is our on-demand commercial vehicle renting service. has a big positive surprise.

guidance.value: Rs 130-160 Cr, tracking to end of range

summary.headline: Delhivery Q2 FY27 revenue crossed Rs 3,066 Cr (+20% YoY) with adjusted PAT of Rs 41 Cr; management says volume guidance of 20-30% is tracking toward the lower end.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as satisfactory against a challenging macro backdrop, with record shipment volume of 325 million (+32% YoY) and revenue of Rs 3,066 Cr (+20% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA came in at Rs 123 Cr (4% of revenue) and PAT at Rs 41 Cr, with cash of Rs 4,676 Cr on the balance sheet. Management said October volumes were strong and that the company is not revising its 20-30% volume growth estimate, which it now sees at the lower end of the range. Newer businesses (Local LCV rental, Direct consumer, International, Saver) were reported ahead of prior expectations, while Express margin is guided to be roughly flat with FY26 and the management said that a 17% full-year margin looks achievable.

financial_highlights.change: Mark-to-market on MF and bond portfolio; excluding MTM, flat

segments.name: Express (PTL)
segments.commentary: Management expects the PTL business to remain a key growth driver and said Express margin is at roughly FY26 levels, with an aim of about 17% full-year margin. PTL realisation improved on contractual revisions and yield gains, and PTL revenue was reported up 23% YoY.

segments.name: Local (LCV rental, on-demand)
segments.commentary: Annualised revenue run-rate crossed Rs 200 Cr across 8 cities, ahead of the Rs 240-250 Cr exit target, and CM breakeven is now seen as early as Q4 vs earlier mid-FY28 expectation.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Standalone run-rate is close to Rs 150 Cr and has reached profitability, which management said came earlier than expected.

segments.name: Direct (consumer)
segments.commentary: Consumer business run-rate is close to Rs 100 Cr after about 15 months of investment. The Saver product is at close to Rs 140 Cr ARR, up 55% QoQ.

segments.name: Supply Chain Services (SCS)
segments.commentary: Management said SCS margins are now normative and the segment has stabilised. The pipeline is intact, but sales cycles have lengthened, and the company is focused on retaining existing clients.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth: management is not revising the 20-30% FY27 estimate and sees the company at the lower end of that range, with October flagged as a strong month.

Express margin: about 17% expected for FY27, with the 16-18% band cited in the shareholder letter; management said 17% is roughly the expected level and flagged no disastrous event that would take it off that level.
Aggregated margin expansion of 130-150 bps conservatively over FY26-FY27 is estimated.
Local (LCV) FY27 loss envelope of Rs 130-160 Cr is maintained, with H1 loss of Rs 67 Cr; management expects to end near the lower end, subject to the contribution trajectory.
Corporate overhead as a percent of revenue is expected to come down, with the 7% level seen taking about 24 months.
Management expects a TAM of about Rs 15,000-20,000 Cr for PTL, with a 15-20% growth target in the medium term.
capex_capacity: Investment in automation: management described tractor trailers, sorters and ASRS as previous paybacks, and said robotics in mid-mile are at pilot stage with payback expected to match earlier TT and sorter cycles.
Company is a 40% shareholder in Falcon Autotech, with self-developed autonomous guided vehicles for in-facility movement.

Company is building out facilities in the top 15 cities for the intra-city NDD (next-day) network. Rapid commerce (dark store model) was stopped after a pilot in 20-30 dark stores across three cities.
Management noted that the company is investing to add capacity in new centres and said it is not looking to be asset light.
demand_pricing: Volume: strong Q2, with October described as a good month and the wider consumption environment holding up despite the macro challenges.

Pricing: about 96-97% of PTL is covered by automatic adjustments for diesel and wage changes. Management said a 2 rupee 40 paisa per-unit increase in PTL yield occurred Q1 to Q2 FY27, roughly half from contractual revisions.
Competition: management expects the marketplace share (about 85% of e-commerce volume) to remain stable, and said the non-e-commerce business is growing faster and is not materially concentrated.
Market size: management said the company is targeting enterprise and non-marketplace clients, with 128,000 enterprises above Rs 5 Cr revenue and 30,000 above Rs 100 Cr in its target base.
Sales productivity: the company is using AI to generate bids and has saved about USD 1 million a year on Google Maps API costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any risk to the 20-30% volume guidance, and where is the growth coming from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were strong, October was a good month, and there is no reason to revise the estimate; it is now at the lower end of the 20-30% range.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: can AI bring unbilled receivables toward zero?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said unbilled revenue is an accounting accrual for partially completed shipments, so AI helps collections and billing accuracy but does not eliminate unbilled.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook and the 16-18% Express band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Express margin of around 17% for FY27, with potential upside from PTL growth and efficiency; Q3 can see some seasonality in yields.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be able to pass on inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said about 96-97% of PTL is automatically covered by fuel and wage indexation, and contract revisions are now shorter, reducing the lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the rapid commerce (intra-city) offering get dialled down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not economic to run separate inventory pools for 2-hour versus 8-hour delivery, so the company is serving those needs through its existing NDD network.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Local (LCV) FY28 loss outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is maintaining the FY27 loss envelope of Rs 130-160 Cr, with H1 at Rs 67 Cr; FY28 guidance will be given later as cities go live.

risks_watch: Express margin: the Q3 festive season and the mix of heavy goods could affect yields, and management noted that the Q1-to-Q2 yield expansion was partly a one-off.
Workforce regulation and wage costs, and climate-driven availability issues, which management says are making Indian labour increasingly uncompetitive on productivity-adjusted terms.
Marketplace concentration: about 85% of volume is e-commerce, and category-level demand shifts (e.g., electronics) could affect volumes.
Local (LCV) and International profitability trajectory, plus the FY28 loss outlook for Local.
SCS sales cycle elongation: the pipeline is intact but conversion has slowed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and cash, with an upbeat view on Local, International and Direct. Cautious on Express margins and FY28 Local losses, and deliberately non-committal on rapid commerce and near-term sales conversion.

adds.what: Facilities being built out in top 15 cities for intra-city NDD (next-day) network; no specific count or capacity given

growth.why: Express revenue growth guided at 16-20% for FY27 (management called it reasonable, a cut), volume growth of 20-30% at the lower end, and Q2 revenue +20% YoY; backing is partial, with PTL yield gains of Rs 2.40/unit and facility build-out in top 15 cities but no specific capacity numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Express margin guided at about 17% (16-18% band), roughly flat with FY26, and aggregated EBITDA margin expansion of 130-150 bps over FY26-FY27 is estimated, but Q2 adjusted EBITDA was only 4% of revenue and Q3 festive yield seasonality and one-off Q1-to-Q2 yield gains are flagged as risks.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Facilities are being built out in the top 15 cities for the intra-city NDD network and management said it is investing to add capacity in new centres, but no count or capacity size was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 shipments were a record 325 million (+32% YoY) and PTL freight volume rose 14.2% YoY to 545K MT; the 20-30% FY27 volume estimate is retained and tracking to the lower end, with October described as strong.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Automation (TT, sorters, ASRS) is described as paid back, and mid-mile robotics are only at pilot stage, while management says it is not looking to be asset light, but no utilisation figure or new capex quantum was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is holding, not raising, the 20-30% volume estimate (only the lower end is flagged), and the Express revenue growth of 16-20% was called reasonable, which is a cut from earlier, not an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Express revenue growth is guided at 16-20% (described as a cut), SCS sales cycles have lengthened, and Q3 festive yield seasonality and heavy-goods mix could pressure Express margin away from 17%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Saver is already at close to Rs 140 Cr ARR (+55% QoQ) and Direct consumer at about Rs 100 Cr run-rate, but no new named product launch with a date was announced; rapid commerce was dropped after a 20-30 dark store pilot.

rows.label: Local (LCV) CM breakeven as early as Q4
rows.why: Local annualised revenue run-rate crossed Rs 200 Cr across 8 cities (vs Rs 240-250 Cr exit target), with H1 FY27 loss of Rs 67 Cr against a Rs 130-160 Cr FY27 envelope expected to end near the lower end.

rows.label: International reached profitability early
rows.why: Standalone International run-rate is close to Rs 150 Cr and has reached profitability earlier than expected.

rows.label: Corporate overhead to 7% of revenue
rows.why: Management expects overhead as a percent of revenue to fall to 7% over about 24 months, with no current level disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes (record 325M shipments, October strong), cash and International/Local/Direct, and cautious on Express margin seasonality, FY28 Local losses and SCS sales conversion; analysts pressed on volume guidance risk, unbilled receivables and whether Express margin of 16-18
